newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares, volume rise on govt prospects.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares, volume rise on govt prospects.

text.p: Istanbul shares rose sharply on Wednesday on liquidity inflow and prospects of a new government to replace the ruling Islamist-led coalition, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 closed 42 points, or 2.76 percent higher at 1,565. Trade volume jumped to 34.06 trillion lira ($243.3 million) from Tuesday's 19.90 trillion ($142.5 million).
"The market began buying on the expectation that the present government will go and the expectation of an alternative government," said Hasan Soydan from Garanti securities.
The index's gains totalled 6.7 percent so far this week. Daily trade volume was at its highest level since March 24.
Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan went into an unannounced meeting with his coalition partner and deputy prime minister Tansu Ciller amid a deepening political crisis.
Ciller earlier suggested elections as a solution to the dispute over Islamist activism after Tuesday's cabinet meeting which was the first in eight weeks.
The coalition has been under pressure since a February National Security Council (NSC) meeting when the secularist military demanded measures to fight rising Islamist zeal.

"There was buying on the expectation of a new government today. If activity seen in shares of energy and state firms since Monday spills over to the whole market tomorrow, we may reach the index's 1,600 level," said Mursel Yildiz from Vakif securities.
"But selling may emerge if an expectation flares that the government will continue as it is," he added.
